why: Repositories waiting on a first judging pass. [CORPUS-REGISTER-COVERAGE] A repository cannot become a register until a judge has ruled on its pairs, and a judge cannot rule on pairs until a comparison has produced two reports for it — so a repository that is not yet judged still has to be scanned. This file is that queue: the comparison scans every register plus everything here, and `make judging-folder` turns each into a workspace. When the verdicts come back, the repository moves into corpus/register/ and out of this list. Every entry is pinned to a full commit id for the same reason a register is: the judge and the scan must read identical source.

repositories.name: Giraffe
repositories.why: F# is judged on FSharp.Data alone, a large library of type providers. Giraffe is a small web framework of handlers and routing combinators, so the F# register gains a repository of visibly different size and style.

repositories.name: Osprey
repositories.why: Osprey has no register at all. Its own repository is the largest body of hand-written Osprey there is: compiler examples, the hunt and LLM packages in both the default `.osp` and ML `.ospml` flavours, and a hand-written C runtime, so one pass also gives C its first judged pairs.

repositories.name: jq
repositories.why: C has no register. jq is a mid-sized hand-written C program, an interpreter with its own parser, bytecode compiler and allocator, full of the error-path and cleanup ladders C duplicates by copying.

repositories.name: hiredis
repositories.why: A small C client library of a visibly different size and style from jq: protocol readers, sync and async connection paths and adapters for several event loops, which repeat set-up and teardown by design.

repositories.name: clap
repositories.why: Rust has one CLEARLY OUT across three registers. clap is a large argument-parsing library with derive macros and many builder variants, a different shape from ripgrep's search code and tokio's runtime.

repositories.name: trpc
repositories.why: TypeScript has no CLEARLY OUT at all. tRPC is a typed RPC monorepo of adapters and client links that repeat set-up per framework, so a pass can rule on look-alikes that are not copies.

repositories.name: riverpod
repositories.why: Dart has one CLEARLY OUT. Riverpod is a provider framework with many parallel provider families and generated-code tests, a different style from bloc and dio.

repositories.name: MediatR
repositories.why: C# rests on Polly plus a short serilog pass. MediatR is a small mediator library with parallel request, notification and stream handler pipelines, a visibly smaller size.

repositories.name: httpx
repositories.why: Python's CLEARLY IN rests on click and django. httpx is a mid-sized HTTP client whose sync and async transports mirror each other, a classic near-copy hunting ground.

repositories.name: Argu
repositories.why: F# has 13 CLEARLY IN, all from FSharp.Data, and giraffe has none agreed. Argu is a small, idiomatic argument parser, a third size and style.

repositories.name: libuv
repositories.why: A large C library beside jq and hiredis: per-platform implementations of the same event-loop primitives under src/unix and src/win, where some repetition is required and some is copied.
